rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a surface treatment (polishing/annealing) to modify defect density on Q235 steel, while the target paper applies an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating via APS and annealing on SS316L. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions—one is a surface modification of the base metal, the other is a coating deposition.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses 3.5 wt% NaCl solution at room temperature and 60–80°C, whereas the target paper uses 3.5 wt% H2SO4 for electrochemical tests and 900°C cyclic hot corrosion with Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures. The environments and temperature regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis focuses on defect sites (grain boundaries, inclusions) acting as anodic sites and preventing passivation, while the target paper's mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase strengthening, and formation of Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides from the HEA coating. These are different classes of mechanism—one is defect-driven dissolution, the other is protective oxide formation from a coating.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced corrosion current density and pitting for defect-reduced Q235 steel, while the target paper predicts higher microhardness, higher polarization resistance, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain for the coated and annealed SS316L. The properties and directions are not comparable.
